# Travel and Expense Policy

## Booking Travel

All business travel (flights, hotels, rental cars) should be booked through
the company's approved travel portal, which provides negotiated corporate
rates. Flights under 6 hours should be booked in economy class; flights over
6 hours may be booked in premium economy with manager approval. Hotel
bookings should not exceed the per-city rate cap listed in the travel
portal.

## Expense Reporting

Expense reports must be submitted within 14 days of the trip's end date,
with itemized receipts attached for any single expense over $25. Reports are
submitted through the expense system and routed to the employee's manager
for approval, then to finance for reimbursement.

## Meals

Employees are reimbursed for reasonable meal expenses while traveling on
company business, up to a daily cap of $75 (breakfast $15, lunch $20, dinner
$40). Alcohol is reimbursable only when part of a client entertainment
expense, up to a $50 per-person limit, and requires manager pre-approval.

## Ground Transportation

Rideshare, taxi, and public transit costs to and from airports, client
sites, or between meetings are reimbursable. Mileage for personal vehicle
use on company business is reimbursed at the current IRS standard mileage
rate.

## Non-Reimbursable Expenses

The company does not reimburse personal entertainment, in-flight
upgrades booked outside the approved travel portal, spa or minibar charges,
traffic or parking fines, or travel companion costs unless pre-approved by
an HR director.
